title: RWB-S6-E6009-APP: the put-back review has no published operation, its claim window, claim reason and realized-recovery figure have no field, column or event, its consumed contracts have no plan row, and two of its four criteria execute rules owned by sibling stories
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.4, R5.5, R5.6, R7.3 and R9; split plan slices RWB-S6-E6009-APP and RWB-S6-E6009-CON; context pack S6 rwb-debtsale (service row, ownership rows, Architecture v5 slides 3, 4, 5, 8 and 13, Temporal and Drools slides 5, 12 and 13); legacy RWB-E6-009; FSD S6 Debt sale v3 A2.13, A2.12, A2.11, A1.4, Requirements served and Screens; TSD S6 Debt sale v2 T2, T3.1 to T3.3, T4, T5.2, T5.3, T6.1, T6.2 and T-A.1 and T-A.2; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-DS-29 and R-DS-34 to R-DS-39; Event and Messaging Design v4 row EV-23; Recovery Workbench Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 row FEAT-DBS-13
description: (1) TSD S6 appendix T-A publishes five operations for S6 and none is a claim, claim-review or claim-decision operation; the two endpoint rows of the legacy story are API-S6-003 POST /debt-sale-lots/{lotId}/award and API-S6-004 GET /partner/data-room/{lotId}, which belong to RWB-S6-E6005-APP and RWB-S6-E5026-APP, so the step has no provided surface. (2) The buyer claim arrives through no published contract: TSD S6 T5.2 names the cross-module interfaces only, the partner channel and its DMZ gateway have no story row, in the plan or in the platform epics or in the X rows of this slice. (3) The claim window of R-DS-34 and R-DS-39 has no length in any source, no parameter name and no column; R-DS-35 carries a 10-working-day review timer and R-DS-29 a 5-working-day transfer timer, but neither is the window. (4) TSD S6 T3.1 carries no claim reason, claim date, claim reference or claim-window column on debt_sale_lot or debt_sale_account; the only claim column is put_back_status with LOV-PUTBACK. (5) R-DS-34 and R-DS-39 record realized recovery by lot and by buyer, but neither table carries such a column, the service's only contracted event is EV-23 LotAwarded, and DP-17 removes the data lake and Power BI that the legacy rule row names. (6) AC2 is R-DS-29, the transfer step of RWB-S6-E6007-APP, and AC3 starts from GL_POSTED, which R-DS-30 and R-DS-31 create in RWB-S6-E6008-APP; the effects of R-DS-36 and R-DS-37, the settlement adjustment and the derecognition reversal, are rwb-payment's and the GL story's, while the plan assigns the four criteria to this key. (7) The plan gives H = RWB-S6-E6009-CON, RWB-PLT-E1027-CON and RWB-PLT-N001-CON with C, I and X empty, while the step consumes the rwb-partner claim and sale terms, the rwb-case state and move, the rwb-access right and the rwb-decision package and parameter, so five rows are class C in fact and have no plan row. (8) DP-06 (parameter), DP-08 (access guard) and DP-09 (outbox) are absent from the pattern set although the step reads a parameter, checks a right and holds a library outbox object. (9) The W-MAP wave of EP06 is 4 while the service's Arch v5 wave is 3. (10) The legacy AC2 and AC3 name states of two sibling features, so the criteria are proved here on fakes and the state owners are named.
evidence: split plan slice RWB-S6-E6009-APP with three H rows and empty C, I and X; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-06, DP-08, DP-09 and DP-17 rows; context pack ownership rows (debt_sale_lot and debt_sale_account, S6; 5 REST operations; event EV-23; workflow DebtSaleWorkflow); TSD S6 T-A.1 (five operations, no claim operation) and T-A.2; TSD S6 T3.1 and T3.2 (LOV-PUTBACK NONE, CLAIMED, ACCEPTED, REJECTED; LOV-LOT-STATUS); Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-DS-29, R-DS-34, R-DS-35, R-DS-36, R-DS-37, R-DS-38 and R-DS-39; Event and Messaging Design v4 row EV-23 (only event of Debt sale); FSD S6 A2.13 and Requirements served REQ-S6-009; Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 FEAT-DBS-13; legacy RWB-E6-009 Data, Endpoints, Screen and states, Permission checks, Validation and messages and Test cases
area: Dependency, contract surface, parameter, reporting and subject ownership
proposed: Keep the plan's H, C, I and X rows as they stand and record the five consumed rows as class C in fact with their placeholders; declare no provided operation and reach the step through the lot read and the data room read of its siblings; read the claim window as a versioned parameter with a placeholder for its length and its operation name; hold the realized recovery on the account selling_price and the closed lot and serve it on the lot read, and allocate a reporting contract or event in a later story; keep wave 4 and record the W-MAP conflict once for S6 and EP06; keep the four criteria here and fake the transfer and posting of RWB-S6-E6007-APP and RWB-S6-E6008-APP

title: RWB-S6-E6009-CON: the claim element, the claim-window parameter, the realized-recovery element, the consumed operation names and the event set have no published baseline
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.4, R5.5, R7.2 and R9; split plan slice RWB-S6-E6009-CON; context pack S6 rwb-debtsale; legacy RWB-E6-009; FSD S6 Debt sale v3 A2.13, Requirements served and Screens; TSD S6 Debt sale v2 T2, T3.1, T3.2, T4, T5.2, T5.3, T6.1 and T-A.1 and T-A.2; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-DS-29 and R-DS-34 to R-DS-39; Event and Messaging Design v4 row EV-23
description: (1) The rwb-partner claim and sale-terms read, the rwb-case state read and case-move answer, the rwb-access authorise call and the rwb-decision package and parameter read publish no operation name, so five consumed rows carry placeholders. (2) No source publishes a REST operation that moves a case state on behalf of a stage; the case boundary is the child workflow's stage outcome and any case-move operation carries a placeholder. (3) TSD S6 T-A.2 gives status codes with no message id per condition, so each condition is bound to a message of the legacy and FSD set. (4) TSD S6 T3.1 gives physical types but publishes no OpenAPI element, so the element names, required flags and formats are fixed by the baseline and not copied from a source; the claim element and the realized-recovery element have no column behind them at all. (5) The claim window has no length and no parameter row, so the parameter element carries a placeholder. (6) TSD S6 T5.3 declares only LotAwarded published and the event catalogue declares only EV-23 for the service, so there is no claim, lot-close or recovery event to declare or consume. (7) The plan's C, I and X rows of this slice are empty while the contract declares five consumed rows.
evidence: TSD S6 T-A.1 operations API-S6-001 to API-S6-005 with no claim operation and T-A.2 error lists 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 and 503 without message ids; TSD S6 T3.1 and T3.2 field lists and LOV-PUTBACK; TSD S6 T5.2 and T5.3; Event and Messaging Design v4 row EV-23; context pack connection-matrix row S6 (Temporal to P7, Temporal and event to P5 and P8, Temporal to P2); FSD S6 A2.13.3.1 and Requirements served; legacy RWB-E6-009 messages MSG-S6-001, MSG-GEN-001, MSG-P4-002 and MSG-P7-003
area: Contract surface, element shapes and interface names
proposed: Publish the baseline with the placeholders, bind every error condition to one message id of section 14, declare the case boundary as the child workflow's input, signals and stage outcome, declare the claim-window parameter as a versioned value with no length, declare the realized recovery on the lot read only, confirm the operation names with their owners before the tag, and record the tag date in the contract README
